newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Range-bound T-bonds stagnate volatilities.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Range-bound T-bonds stagnate volatilities.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were mostly steady in late trade as the underlying market drifted in relatively narrow ranges, still convalescing from Friday's selloff, dealers said.
"The market is still digesting last week's breaks," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.

While fear of a further major slide in the near term was abating, the bond market appeared to be wary of making a big move ahead of Wednesday's U.S. producer price index and Thursday's consumer price index, traders said.
March futures were unchanged at 114-14/32 in late trade.
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options stood at about 9.75 percent, up 0.1 point from Monday's close but looking feeble and already at historically low levels.
A bank affiliate trader at CBOT said volatilities were the softest for the 10-year area.
Implied volatility for March 10-year T-note futures options was off a quarter point to around 6.1 percent, the lowest level in about a year, he said.
Among the larger trades of the day in T-bonds, a commercial firm was seen buying 500 legs of January 115/116 call spread in a one-by-two ratio.
An investment bank was seen selling 2,000 lots of March 118/120 call spread, while a second bank bought 500 March 114 straddles and a third bought 1,000 March 110 puts.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, volatilities were steady to softer, with front-end futures grinding to a halt.
Implied volatilities for March and June Eurodollar futures options stood at 9.8 and 13.8 percent, virtually unchanged from Monday.
People who wanted to build up positions ahead of the PPI and CPI numbers have probably already done so and volume was light, traders said.
"Proprietary trading seems to be focusing on the longer end (rather than Eurodollars)," said a Eurodollar trader at an investment bank at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Most traders expect the inflation numbers to be benign and the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates steady at the upcoming December 17 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

But they cited market rumors that Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, who last week expressed concerns about "irrational exuberance" in asset markets, could tighten bank reserve requirements or take some other measures to check asset price inflation.
"There's talk that he might do it in a very underhanded way for the time being," the CME trader said. He said the rumors at least reflected the degree of nervousness in the market.

One firm was seen buying 5,000 lots of December 94.50/94.62 call spread. The spread was seen used to roll down the strike price of a long position that would soon expire. December contracts expire next Monday and the deep out-of-the-money 94.62 contract had open interest of 5,221 contracts at the start of the day. December futures stood unchanged at 94.48, near the cash-parity rate.
